title: `one()` and `only()` raise ValueError instead of my custom exception
spec:
This is the more-itertools library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `python3 run_tests.py`.

`one` and `only` let you pass `too_short` / `too_long` to raise instead of the default `ValueError`. That is ignored when the exception instance is falsy:

```python
import more_itertools as mi
class FalsyError(Exception):
    def __bool__(self):
        return False

mi.one([1, 2], too_long=FalsyError('too many'))
# expected: FalsyError('too many')
# actual:   ValueError: Expected exactly one item in iterable, but got 1, 2, and perhaps more.
```

`mi.one([], too_short=FalsyError('too few'))` and `mi.only([1, 2], too_long=FalsyError('too many'))` fail the same way. Whatever was passed should be raised; only when nothing was given should the default `ValueError` apply.

Related: when I do pass `too_long`, the items are still `repr`'d for a message that is never shown. If an item's `__repr__` raises, `mi.one([x, y], too_long=OverflowError)` raises that `RuntimeError` instead of `OverflowError` (same for `only`). With a custom exception, the items should not be `repr`'d at all.
acceptance: A falsy custom `too_short` / `too_long` is raised by `one`, and `too_long` by `only`
Passing `too_long` never calls `repr` on the items
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
